light.notes: bg base2, paper base3, chip base2 (the palette has two light tones); border derived (base2 toward base1); text-1 base01 emphasised, text-2 base00 body, text-3 base1; amber is orange, purple is violet, series two is cyan and four is magenta. blue and violet are darkened six points and one point of lightness so white ink reads 4.5 on them. The roles derived from both stay pinned to the published values. base01 ink reads under 1.7 on every accent, and a green or yellow dark enough for white ink is a different colour from the published pair, so both keep white at 3.2 (MAD-378)

dark.notes: bg base03, paper base02, chip base02; border derived (base02 toward base01); text-1 base1, text-2 base0, text-3 base01. The palette has one value per accent. red, orange, and violet are lifted a few points of lightness (52% to 58%, 44% to 48%, 60% to 63%) to meet 3:1 as text on base02 (MAD-372). blue is lifted from 49% to 53% so base03 ink reads 4.5 on it (MAD-376). The roles derived from the four stay pinned to the published values. A fill light enough to read on base02 is too light for white ink at 4.5. base03 ink needs a fill at luminance 0.265, which red, orange, and violet reach only by leaving the published hues. So those three keep white ink under 4.5: 4.0 on red and orange, where base03 reads 3.8, and 3.8 on violet. On violet base03 reads 3.9 by the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) ratio but far worse by the Advanced Perceptual Contrast Algorithm (APCA), so on-purple is pinned white to match its siblings
